newsitem.title: UK: European vegetable oil close with minimal changes - Feb 13.
newsitem.headline: European vegetable oil close with minimal changes - Feb 13.

text.p: Closing European vegetable oil prices were little changed on Thursday from the previous close.
Trading was light throughout most of the day with the palm oil market still hampered by holidays in the Far East.
"A lot of people won't be back until Monday in Malaysia and hopefully business will start to pick up then," said a trader.
Palm oil prices were mixed at the European close after a the post holiday rally on the KLCE fizzled out.
However, traders said they did not think the run of firm palm oil prices was over and expect further gains in the short term.

"Palm oil will stay firm for the time being because speculators will play on the seasonally low production, but sooner or later there will have to be a downward correction if palm oil is to be competitive in the market place," said one trader.
Crude palm oil cif Europe closed unchanged to $5 up with no outright trade reported.
However, Feb traded at $587.50 a tonne in a switch with Apr/Jun at $572.50 and Feb also traded in a switch with Mar at a $5 difference.
Coconut oil finished around $2.50 lower after Jan/Feb traded at $782.50 and $785 and Apr/May at $757.50 a tonne cif in mainly dealer trading.
Palmkernel oil closed $2.50 down and tradeless.
Soft oils were mostly lower following early falls in Chicago with soy oil ending the session one guilder down to 0.50 guilders up and rape oil unchanged to 0.50 guilders lower.
In thin trading Mar soyoil fetched 98.25 guilders a 100 kilos fob ex-mill
EU sunflower oil closed around $2.50 up after Mar traded at $490 and Apr at $495 and $500 a tonne ex-tank with a five ports option.
